## My Journey in Science

I am interested in how genomes record adaptation across time and space. My work combines evolutionary biology, quantitative genetics, and reproducible data workflows to study biological complexity under changing environments.

I enjoy building practical pipelines that turn raw sequencing and phenotypic datasets into interpretable biological insights. This includes statistical modeling, machine learning, and careful data curation, especially in crop and ecological genomics.

Teaching and mentoring are central to how I work. I value clear explanation, open workflows, and helping students connect computation with biological questions.
